Reannotate gene IDs to a common namespace

Source: R/02_harmonize.R
mx_reannotate.Rd

Converts the gene identifiers of one or more studies to a single namespace (gene symbol, Ensembl gene ID or Entrez ID) so that studies can be compared gene by gene.

Usage

mx_reannotate(
  studies,
  org = "Homo sapiens",
  target_id = c("SYMBOL", "ENSEMBL", "ENTREZID"),
  from_id = NULL,
  mapping = NULL,
  duplicates = c("max_mean", "sum", "drop"),
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)

Arguments

studies

A named list of metaXpressStudy objects, or a single study.

org

Organism: "Homo sapiens" (default; org.Hs.eg.db), "Mus musculus" (org.Mm.eg.db) or "Rattus norvegicus" (org.Rn.eg.db). Ignored when mapping is given.

target_id

Target identifier: "SYMBOL" (default), "ENSEMBL" or "ENTREZID".

from_id

Source identifier type, or NULL (default) to detect it per study.

mapping

Optional data.frame with columns from and to giving the ID mapping to use instead of an org.*.eg.db package.

duplicates

How to collapse several source IDs mapping to one target: "max_mean" (default), "sum" or "drop".

BPPARAM

A BiocParallelParam. Default: BiocParallel::SerialParam().

Value

The studies with translated rownames (same type as the input: a list or a single study). A per-study mapping summary is printed.

Details

Processing steps for each study:

  1. Ensembl version suffixes are removed (ENSG00000141510.17 becomes ENSG00000141510), as are Ensembl _PAR_Y pseudo-autosomal duplicates.

  2. The source identifier type is detected from all IDs by majority (Ensembl, Entrez or symbol), or set with from_id.

  3. IDs are mapped with the organism's org.*.eg.db package, or with a user-supplied mapping table (any organism, offline).

  4. Unmapped IDs are dropped and reported.

  5. When several source IDs map to the same target ID, they are collapsed with duplicates: "max_mean" keeps the most highly expressed source row (default, as in WGCNA's collapseRows); "sum" adds counts (appropriate when the source rows are disjoint features of one gene); "drop" removes all ambiguous genes.

The original identifier of every retained row is stored in rowData(study)$source_id.

References

Pages, H. et al. AnnotationDbi: manipulation of SQLite-based annotations in Bioconductor. https://bioconductor.org/packages/AnnotationDbi

Miller, J.A. et al. (2011) Strategies for aggregating gene expression data: the collapseRows R function. BMC Bioinformatics, 12, 322. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-12-322

See also

mx_align_genes, mx_gene_sets

Examples

counts <- matrix(c(10, 20, 30, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 7, 7, 7),
                 nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
                 dimnames = list(c("ENSG00000141510.17", "ENSG00000012048.23",
                                   "ENSG00000999999.1"),
                                 paste0("S", 1:4)))
meta  <- data.frame(condition = c("control", "control", "case", "case"))
study <- metaXpressStudy(counts, meta, accession = "local")
map   <- data.frame(from = c("ENSG00000141510", "ENSG00000012048"),
                    to   = c("TP53", "BRCA1"))
out <- mx_reannotate(study, mapping = map)
#>   local: ENSEMBL -> SYMBOL | 3 IDs, 1 unmapped (33.3%), 0 rows collapsed (max_mean), 2 genes
rownames(out)
#> [1] "TP53"  "BRCA1"
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(out)$source_id
#> [1] "ENSG00000141510.17" "ENSG00000012048.23"
